place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 柴房 · 腊月初九
place.en: Chending Temple · The woodshed · Ninth of the twelfth month

setup.zh: 大比第二天，你从外门的大通铺搬进内门西廊。理储物袋，理出邹青松那只赤铜葫芦和七八瓣盾片——废物。
setup.en: The day after the contest you move from the outer court's long bunk to the inner court's west wing. Sorting the storage pouch turns up Zou Qingsong's red-copper gourd and seven or eight shield shards — rubbish.

recap.zh: 搬屋那天，你把赤铜葫芦和盾片扔进饭桶，图个干净；它吐出一口剑，剑脊上自己刻着：火柴。
recap.en: The day you moved, you tossed the red-copper gourd and the shield shards into the Rice Tub just to be rid of them; it spat out a sword with its own name cut in the spine: Matchstick.

zh: 一只空葫芦，七八瓣盾片——废物。
en: The day after the contest: moving house.
An empty gourd, seven or eight shards — rubbish.
Into the Rice Tub, just to be rid of them.

story.zh: 搬屋那几天，他把储物袋倒了个底朝天，一样一样理，理出两样废物：邹青松那只赤铜葫芦，葫芦嘴敞着，肚里空空的；那七八瓣赤铜盾片，叮叮当当一小堆。
story.en: In the days of the move, he turned the storage pouch out onto the boards to sort it, one thing at a time; two pieces of rubbish came out: Zou Qingsong's red-copper gourd, cork still in, nothing in its belly; and the seven or eight shards of the red-copper shield, a little clinking heap.

label.en: Toss them into the Rice Tub, just to be rid of them

exits.means: tosses the red-copper gourd and the shield shards into the Rice Tub to be rid of them, wanting nothing; it spits out a plain sword, Matchstick

story.zh:
他摸进柴房，按开饭桶，一股脑儿倒了进去，心里什么也没想——扔了干净。

饭桶嚼了很久。「咯嘣」，「咯嘣」，嚼一阵，歇一歇，像一个没牙的老头啃一块冻硬了的饼；歇一回，吸他一口气，吸到第五口，他眼前一阵一阵发黑。末了，盖子「咔哒」一弹，一道红光窜出来，「笃」的一声，钉在了门板上，剑柄还在嗡嗡地颤。小狰一头扎进了柴堆。

他拔出剑来，门板上只留一道缝，顺着木纹一直裂到底，齐得像刨过。一口剑，三尺来长，剑身暗红，是那葫芦和盾片的铜色，火纹一道也没有了；剑脊上一溜锤印，坑坑洼洼，像镇上铁匠铺里学徒打坏了的。灌一丝灵力进去，剑身上浮起薄薄一层光，像一层油——是件法器，最寻常的那一种。剑脊近柄那一截，锤印当中歪歪扭扭刻着两个字：火柴；底下一行小字：剑起火升，攻守兼备。
story.en:
He slipped into the woodshed, pressed the Rice Tub open, and tipped the lot in, wanting nothing at all — just to be rid of it.

The Rice Tub chewed a long time. *Crunch*, *crunch* — chewing a while and resting, like a toothless old man at a frozen flatbread; every rest it took a mouthful of his qi, and by the fifth his sight was going black in waves. At last the lid sprang open with a *clack*, a streak of red shot out — *thock* — and stuck in the door, the hilt still humming. Little Zheng dived headfirst into the woodpile.

He drew the sword out, leaving only a seam in the board that split clean down the grain, as straight as if planed. A sword, three feet or so, its blade a dull red — the copper of the gourd and the shards — with not one line of the fire pattern left; down the spine a row of hammer marks, pitted and uneven, like a botched piece from an apprentice at the town smithy. He sent a thread of qi into it, and a thin light rose on the blade like a film of oil — an artifact, of the commonest kind. Near the hilt, among the hammer marks, two crooked characters were cut into the spine: *Matchstick*; and under them a line of small ones: *The sword rises, the fire climbs; attack and guard in one.*
